title: Recover a caught sample carrier with coordinated two-arm motion
instruction: Move the sample carrier onto the receiving stand, keeping the samples upright and contained. If it catches, stop and free it without forcing or tipping it, then complete the transfer.
context: Laboratory transport of capped dummy samples with a retaining lip that obstructs one carrier ear. Clearing the visible obstruction before lifting is valid.
setup: A 120 by 240 mm carrier holds four independent rigid capped dummy tubes, each 30 mm in diameter with a 72 mm body. Two 64 mm grip bars are 380 mm apart, each on a passive revolute connection. An orange retaining lip overlaps one ear at the source stand. A second stand is 195 mm away along the transfer direction. Original primitive assets and the YAM station. The source has two 165 by 18 by 18 mm longitudinal polymer strips ending at x=335 mm, friction coefficient 0.10 as an uncalibrated design parameter.
scoring: Historical zero if carrier tilt exceeds 12 degrees or any sampled bottom-circumference point exits the carrier bounds. 0.5 when the complete carrier is clear of the source stand, level within 5 degrees, with all samples contained and upright within 10 degrees. 1.0 when the carrier is within 10 mm and 5 degrees of its receiving pose, samples upright within 10 degrees, both grippers released and clear, and stable for 1 second.
fidelity: Rigid carrier, capped rigid dummy samples and fixed retaining lip. Passive revolute grip bars approximate folding supports. No liquids, material deformation or actuator faults. Thresholds are design values; no claim that every real carrier requires two hands.
scores: Dream-1-beta: 0.0 in 2400 control steps; scripted physical demo: 1.0 in 700 steps. Seed 42, fixed layout.
reset_notes: Fresh scene reset restores the fixed layout and clears all safety and stability history. Seed 42; object jitter disabled.
